\title{Gauged U(2) Spin-Zero Superfluid of 16 Component Dirac Fermions on 7+1 Spacetime}

\author{Patrick Lee Nash}
\affiliation{PROJECT spacetimes}

\date{November 16, 2026}

\begin{abstract}
On the eight-dimensional Minkowski spacetime of signature $7+1$ a single 16-component Dirac
field cannot form a spin-zero pair: both charge-conjugation matrices $C^\pm_{1671}$ are
symmetric, so $\psi^{1T}_{U2}C^\pm_{1671}\psi^1_{U2}$ vanishes for an anticommuting field
$\psi^1_{U2}$. A pair of total spin zero therefore needs
a doublet $\Psi_{U2}=(\psi^1_{U2},\psi^2_{U2})$ in the antisymmetric combination, and the
symmetry of that combination fixes a new gauge group, $U(2)_{U2}$, with a covariant derivative
modelled on that of the electroweak theory. We give the Lagrangian with quadratic and quartic
self-interactions, the self-interacting Dirac equations, their mean-field spinor solutions in
closed form, and the effective potential of the superfluid. Its minimum breaks
$U(2)_{U2}\to SU(2)_{U2}$: in the vacuum above a critical coupling, at finite density for any
attraction. After the breaking the $U(1)_{U2}$ boson acquires the mass $g'_{U2}f_{U2}$, the
$SU(2)_{U2}$ bosons stay massless, and a neutral scalar, the amplitude mode $\sigma_{U2}$,
appears with mass exactly $2\Delta_{U2}$; its exchange carries the attraction in the spin-zero
channel. All {{GEN:nchecks_rust}} statements that the results rest on are machine-checked.
\end{abstract}
